title: PARTITION BY and Window Ordering
learningObjectives: Explain how PARTITION BY divides a window into independent groups.
Use a partitioned aggregate to calculate totals and averages per group.
Distinguish ORDER BY inside OVER from the outer query ORDER BY.
Use a tie-breaker to make ordered window calculations deterministic.
Preserve individual rows while calculating per-group summaries.

understand.concept: PARTITION BY divides rows into independent windows. ORDER BY inside OVER defines the logical order used by order-sensitive window calculations. The outer query's ORDER BY controls only how the final result is displayed.
understand.whyItMatters: Partitions support per-department totals, per-customer running calculations and comparisons within a group without losing individual rows.
understand.analogy: A window calculation is like adding a running commentary to each row while keeping the original list intact.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not represent SQL partition rules, frame boundaries, tie handling or optimizer behaviour.

explain.narrative:
## PARTITION BY
PARTITION BY divides the input into groups. A window aggregate is calculated separately for each partition, but each source row remains visible.

## ORDER BY inside OVER
ORDER BY inside OVER defines the order used by ranking and ordered window calculations. It is not the same as the outer ORDER BY, which controls display order.

## Deterministic ordering
When ties are possible, add a stable tie-breaker such as a unique id if the function requires a deterministic row sequence. A window order does not guarantee final display order unless the outer query also has ORDER BY.

examples.title: Create regional sales data
examples.code: CREATE TABLE win14_regions (sale_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, region TEXT NOT NULL, salesperson TEXT NOT NULL, amount INTEGER NOT NULL);
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates create regional sales data with SQLite window functions. Check the window definition and row order.

examples.title: Insert two regions
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates insert two regions with SQLite window functions. Check the window definition and row order.

examples.title: Calculate a total per region while preserving each sale
examples.code: SELECT salesperson, region, amount, SUM(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS region_total FROM win14_regions ORDER BY region, salesperson;
examples.expectedOutput: Asha | East | 100 | 150; Bilal | East | 50 | 150; Mira | West | 80 | 100; Noor | West | 20 | 100
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates calculate a total per region while preserving each sale with SQLite window functions. Check the window definition and row order.

examples.title: Calculate average amount per region
examples.code: SELECT salesperson, region, amount, AVG(amount) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS region_average FROM win14_regions ORDER BY region, salesperson;
examples.expectedOutput: Asha | East | 100 | 75.0; Bilal | East | 50 | 75.0; Mira | West | 80 | 50.0; Noor | West | 20 | 50.0
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates calculate average amount per region with SQLite window functions. Check the window definition and row order.

examples.title: Number sales within each region
examples.code: SELECT salesperson, region, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY amount DESC, salesperson) AS region_position FROM win14_regions ORDER BY region, region_position;
examples.expectedOutput: Asha | East | 1; Bilal | East | 2; Mira | West | 1; Noor | West | 2
examples.explanation: This example demonstrates number sales within each region with SQLite window functions. Check the window definition and row order.

practise.guidedTask: Run the regional examples. Explain why each row remains visible and why East and West receive different totals.
practise.independentTask: Create sales data for at least three regions. Calculate each region's total and average, then number sales within each region using a deterministic order.

questions.prompt: Does PARTITION BY collapse rows like GROUP BY?
options: No, it preserves the input rows
Yes, always one row per partition
Only when used with ORDER BY
questions.answer: No, it preserves the input rows

questions.prompt: What does ORDER BY inside OVER control?
options: The logical order used by the window calculation
The physical order of the database file
questions.answer: The logical order used by the window calculation
questions.explanation: The window ORDER BY controls how order-sensitive functions evaluate rows.

questions.prompt: What controls the final displayed order?
questions.explanation: The outer ORDER BY determines the returned row order.

questions.prompt: Why add a unique tie-breaker to window ordering?
options: To make row sequence deterministic when sort values tie
questions.answer: To make row sequence deterministic when sort values tie
questions.explanation: A stable tie-breaker resolves otherwise ambiguous ordering among tied rows.
